_meta.purpose: Publishable rule-change events for the public changes feed.
_meta.separable: Deliberately independent of the mobility determination engine, which is HELD from production. The feed publishes change facts + citations only.
_meta.status_derivation: Structured fields ONLY (rule_changes_on presence + direction). Status is NOT inferred from prose: 27 of 55 records match enacted/proposed/rule signals simultaneously, so a regex label would be a guess. Records whose status cannot be established from structure are not emitted.
_meta.reverification_rule: needs_reverification=true means the effective date has passed and we have NOT re-checked. The page must say 'effective [date]; we re-verify on/after that date' -- never 'is now in effect'.

events.detail: SB26-076 (signed 2026-05-04, Ch. 81) rewrites CRS 12-100-117(2)(a)(I): from 2026-08-12 an individual out-of-state CPA licensed in good standing with principal place of business elsewhere has ALL the same practice privileges as Colorado certificate holders if, at initial licensure, their licensing state required passing the Uniform CPA Exam and a baccalaureate degree (individual-criteria/near-CPA=CPA test replacing the current NASBA-substantial-equivalency test in Rule 1.14); CPAs holding CO practice privileges as of 2024-12-31 are grandfathered, and the board is statutorily barred from requiring any notice, fee, or other submission. Effective-date verification: the act uses Colorado's standard referendum-petition clause (no supermajority immediate-effect mechanism exists in CO), so the remainder of the act takes effect the day after the 90-day post-adjournment period (GA adjourned 2026-05-13); leg.colorado.gov's official bill history lists '08/12/2026 - Effective date'; only section 1 (12-100-108 licensure pathways: BA+2yr experience / BA+30hr+1yr / post-bacc+1yr) is delayed to 2027-01-01. SB26-076 § 3 also narrows the firm-registration exception cross-reference in 12-100-114(1) from '12-100-117(2)' to '12-100-117(2)(a)(II)' (firm incident-to exception only). Source-disagreement flags: (1) Board Rule 1.14 (3 CCR 705-1, current version eff. 12/15/2024) still states the superseded NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalency test; conforming board rulemaking is pending (COCPA reports notice-comment-hearing phase next; hearings to post at dpo.colorado.gov/Accountancy_Program_Info, which itself shows stale 2019-2022 content). (2) COCPA (secondary) claims the mobility provisions take effect only when the board adopts implementing rules — the act's own effective-date clause contains no such condition; act text controls.

events.citation: RSMo § 326.283 (individual practice privilege); RSMo § 326.289 (firm permits); 20 CSR 2010-2.022 (Privilege to Practice)
events.detail: TWO issues. (1) ENACTED CHANGE: SB 1233 (2026), signed by Gov. Kehoe July 2026, repeals the substantial-equivalency test in 326.283 and replaces it with INDIVIDUAL CRITERIA: a valid unrestricted license in good standing from any state, provided that at initial licensure the individual passed the Uniform CPA Exam and met one of three education/experience combos (bachelor's + accounting concentration + 2 yrs experience; bachelor's + 30 hrs + 1 yr; post-baccalaureate degree + 1 yr). Grandfather clause preserves privileges for anyone licensed and holding MO practice privileges as of 2024-12-31. No-notice/no-fee language is retained. Also adds a sole-practitioner/single-member-LLC exemption request from the CPA-title firm-permit requirement (non-attest only). The TAT text has NO emergency clause for the accountancy sections (the only contingent-effective-date section, Section B, covers interior-design repeals 324.406/324.424), so ch. 326 changes take effect on Missouri's constitutional default date 2026-08-28; press coverage (Accounting Today, CFO Dive, Inside Public Accounting) uniformly confirms Aug. 28, 2026. On that date equivalence_test flips from nasba_state_level to individual_criteria. (2) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm_registration_attest: compiled statute 326.289.1(2) (as amended 2020, HB 2046) lets a firm with NO office in Missouri perform attest/compilation WITHOUT a permit if it meets ownership, peer-review, practice-privilege-individual, and lawful-in-home-state conditions; but the board's still-compiled rule 20 CSR 2010-2.022(5) (last amended eff. 2012-06-30, authority cites RSMo Supp. 2011) states attest services for a client with a home office in Missouri must be performed 'through a firm holding a current permit to practice in this state,' and the board's Initial Firm Permit application (form 375-0715) still instructs out-of-state firms on obtaining a permit to provide attest/review/compilation services. Per the conservative rule, firm_registration_attest is recorded TRUE (permit required); the statute's no-permit pathway is quoted in the quotes array. No board rulemaking to conform 2.022 to the 2020 statute or to SB 1233 was pending on the DCI proposed-rules page as of 2026-07-31.

events.citation: Ala. Code § 34-1-7 (practice privilege; Act 2009-620 scheme); Ala. Code §§ 34-1-6, 34-1-10, 34-1-11, 34-1-16(12) (firm registration/permits, attest exception); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04 (Mobility); all as amended by HB59, 2026 Reg. Sess. (Pathways to CPA Act), eff. 2026-10-01
events.detail: HB59 (2026 Reg. Sess., 'Pathways to CPA Act', Rep. Underwood) passed House 20-Jan-26, Senate 22-Jan-26, signed by Gov. Ivey late Jan 2026. Section 3 states a flat effective date: 'This act shall become effective on October 1, 2026.' -- no supermajority/immediate-effect option, so no vote-count analysis needed. It rewrites 34-1-7(a): current law grants practice privilege to any 'person who is licensed as a certified public accountant in another state' (open CPA=CPA, no equivalency test); from 2026-10-01 the individual must ALSO have 'satisfied the educational requirements adopted by rule of the board' -- i.e., Alabama moves to individual-criteria mobility with the education test delegated to board rule. Board rulemaking defining those educational requirements is pending (secondary sources report proposed pathway rules circulating with an Oct 15, 2026 reference); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04 (last amended eff. 2009-12-23) and the board's mobility web page still state only the pre-HB59 open-license test -- not a present-day contradiction because HB59 is not yet effective, but both will be stale on 2026-10-01 unless updated. Firm-side rules (no registration for firms with no Alabama office, including for attest via the 34-1-16(12) exception for individuals practicing under 34-1-7) are carried forward substantively unchanged by HB59. UPDATE (verifier): ASBPA Notice of Intended Action amending Ch. 30-X-4 filed with LSA 2026-05-08 (comment period closed 2026-07-10); it does NOT amend 30-X-3-.04 and does NOT yet supply the 34-1-7(a) education rule for out-of-state privilege holders. HB59 signing date confirmed: Gov. Ivey announced signing 2026-01-30 ("I have signed HB59, the Pathways to CPA Act"); act number still unlocated - open question retained.

events.citation: 59 O.S. § 15.12A (individual practice privilege; firm non-attest privilege at (A)(4)); 59 O.S. § 15.15(A)(3) and § 15.15C (out-of-state firm attest exemption); 59 O.S. § 15.30 (quality/peer review); as amended by Laws 2023, SB 172, c. 26 (eff. 2023-11-01) and Laws 2026, HB 4317, c. 186 (eff. 2026-11-01)
events.detail: HB 4317 (Laws 2026, c. 186) — Oklahoma's UAA 9th-edition rewrite — passed House 83-0 (2026-03-11) and Senate 44-0 (2026-04-29), Governor signed 2026-05-05 (bill history; OSCPA reported May 6). No emergency clause; enrolled act Section 5 states verbatim: 'This act shall become effective November 1, 2026.' It rewrites 59 O.S. 15.12A from the current substantial-equivalency scheme (NASBA-verified jurisdictions presumed equivalent, PLUS a catch-all presumption for licensees of non-verified jurisdictions) to an individual-criteria mobility model: any valid out-of-state CPA/PA license + passed Uniform CPA Exam + at initial licensure met one of three pathways (post-baccalaureate accounting degree + 1 yr experience; bachelor's + 30 extra hours + 1 yr; bachelor's with accounting concentration + 2 yrs). The no-notice/no-fee sentence and the firm non-attest privilege are retained in the new text. Both statute versions are published on OSCN (CiteID 552496 = operative until 2026-10-31; CiteID 385656 = text effective 2026-11-01). Board rulemaking for 2026 ('2026 Regulatory Text' PDF, image-only scan, content unverified) is pending and should be watched. UPDATE (verifier): HB 2736 (Laws 2025, c. 192, eff. 2025-11-01) also amended 59 O.S. 15.8/15.9 exam-eligibility education - prior-wave context, no field change. The 2026-11-01 version of 15.12A appends "Such an individual shall be subject to the requirements in paragraph 3 of this subsection" to the no-notice sentence - post-changeover, the no-notice privilege is expressly conditioned on paragraph-3 compliance. Open question on un-diffed 15.12A(A)(4) CLOSED: the current (2023) compiled text does contain the firm non-attest paragraph with the "without a firm license, permit, or notice to the Board" language (verifier confirmed on CiteID 552496).

events.citation: N.Y. Educ. Law § 7406(2) (practice privilege); §§ 7408, 7410 (firm registration and peer review); 8 NYCRR 70.7
events.detail: Chapter 530 of the Laws of 2025 (S6891B), signed 2025-11-21 and effective 2026-11-21 ('This act shall take effect twelve months after it shall have become a law'), rewrites Educ. Law 7406(2): the current test - licensure by a state the Board of Regents has determined substantially equivalent, or individual qualifications verified by the department - is replaced by individual criteria: valid license in good standing, out-of-state principal place of business, completion of either of the professional education and experience requirements in 7404(1)(2)-(3), and passage of the written examination in 7404(1)(4). NY Senate OpenLegislation already displays both versions of 7406 side by side (pre- and post-2026-11-21) and they AGREE with the enacted bill text, so this is a clean enacted-but-not-yet-effective change, not a source contradiction. Chapter 530 also adds a bachelor's-degree + exam + 2-years-experience licensure pathway. UPDATE (verifier): implementing rulemaking has actively begun - the proposed Part 70 amendment implementing Chapter 530 was published in the State Register for a 60-day comment period, with anticipated adoption at the September 2026 Board of Regents meeting and effective date 2026-11-21 (per the July 29, 2026 NYS Board for Public Accountancy public meeting packet). 8 NYCRR 70.7 itself is not yet conformed.

events.citation: A.R.S. § 32-725 (limited reciprocity privilege; individuals and out-of-state firms); A.R.S. § 32-731 (CPA firm registration); as amended by Laws 2026, Ch. 17 (SB 1181, Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026) eff. 2027-01-01
events.detail: SB 1181 (Laws 2026, Ch. 17, 'Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026') was signed 2026-04-07 and is enacted but NOT YET EFFECTIVE: the act's own Sec. 18 states 'This act is effective from and after December 31, 2026,' i.e. operative 2027-01-01. This in-act delayed date governs (it is later than the session's general effective date of 2026-09-12 after the 2026-06-13 sine die; no emergency clause, so no supermajority vote-count question arises). The act strikes the current A.R.S. 32-725(B)(4) mobility test (licensing jurisdiction requires 150 semester hours + baccalaureate + passed CPA exam + 1 year verified experience, OR individual meets 32-721(C)) and replaces it with: individual holds an out-of-state CPA license AND either (a) meets the qualifications in 32-721(A) (new pathways: baccalaureate+2yrs experience, baccalaureate+30 extra hours+1yr, or postbaccalaureate+1yr) or 32-4302 (Arizona universal-licensure-recognition statute), or (b) holds a valid active CPA registration/certificate/license from any jurisdiction as of December 31, 2024 (grandfather clause). The no-notice/no-fee provision (32-725(D)) and the out-of-state-firm no-registration provision (32-725(G)) are carried forward unchanged (Ch. 17 also adds out-of-state firms to the 'limited reciprocity privilege' definition). The board's Mobility page currently matches the in-force pre-2027 statute (no stale-page disagreement today), but will need updating at the changeover. UPDATE (verifier): Board Notice of Proposed Expedited Rulemaking (July 2026) implements Laws 2026 Ch. 17 - outlines required accounting/related course hours for certification (which feed the 32-721(A) qualifications the NEW 2027 mobility test cross-references) and reduces reciprocity verifications to one jurisdiction; oral proceeding 2026-08-24, final text pending - recheck after adoption. DIFFLAB WARNING: the board News page headline styles the act '(Effective December 31, 2026)' - that is a paraphrase of the act's 'from and after December 31, 2026' clause; the operative date remains 2027-01-01. Do not let an alert on that phrasing trigger a date change. Board also ran 2025-2026 expedited rule updates on peer review (R4-1-454, May 2025) and CPE (May 2026).

P.A. 104-0228 (HB2459, signed 2025-08-15, eff. 2026-01-01) retitled 225 ILCS 450/5.2 from 'Substantial equivalency' to 'Enhanced mobility' and REPLACED the NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency test with: (1) issuing state's licensure requirements equivalent to the criteria in Section 14, or (2) individual petition to the Public Accountant Registration and Licensure Committee for an equivalency determination of education, exam, and experience. NOTE: the prior-research claim that IL 'adopted NASBA NQAS state-level equivalency' is BACKWARDS - the enrolled act DELETES the NQAS language (shown stricken in the act). The prior-research claim that the enrolled act and compiled ILCS state DIFFERENT tests could not be reproduced: researcher AND independent adversarial verifier each fetched the enrolled act's raw HTML with strike/underline markup preserved and the compiled ILCS text; both state the SAME new Section-14-equivalence/petition test (compiled source line: 'P.A. 103-309, eff. 1-1-24; 104-228, eff. 1-1-26'). The apparent contradiction arises when the act's STRICKEN NQAS text loses strikethrough formatting during text extraction and reads as live text - both versions are reproduced verbatim in the evidence quotes; human review of the enrolled act PDF should confirm. Still genuinely in flux: (a) Section 14 licensure criteria - the referent of the 5.2(a)(1) equivalence test - gain two new pathways on 2027-01-01 (bachelor's in accounting + 2 yrs experience; master's or bachelor's + 30 accounting hrs + 1 yr), which will shift which states are 'equivalent'; (b) IDFPR's administrative rules (68 Ill. Adm. Code 1420) contain no mobility/practice-privilege section and have not been updated for P.A. 104-0228 (1420.35 Temporary Practice is repealed) - rulemaking is likely; (c) the entire Public Accounting Act is scheduled to be repealed 2029-01-01 (sunset).

events.citation: Ind. Code § 25-2.1-4-10 (individual practice privilege, no notice); Ind. Code §§ 25-2.1-12-5 and 25-2.1-12-2 (firm permit required for attest services/CPA title use); Ind. Code § 25-2.1-5-8 and 872 IAC 1-6-9 (peer review as condition of firm permit renewal)
events.detail: HEA 1143 (P.L. 85-2025, signed 2025-04-16) amends IC 25-2.1-3-2 to add a bachelor's-degree + 2-years-experience licensure pathway, effective 2027-01-01 (the board's own Nonrule Policy Document 25-467 states 'this language will not take effect until January 1, 2027'). The mobility statute IC 25-2.1-4-10 itself was NOT amended (last amended P.L.190-2007). To bridge the gap, the Board adopted Nonrule Policy Document 25-467 'Substantial Equivalency Clarification' (adopted 2025-09-12 by 3-2-0 vote, effective on Indiana Register publication 2025-10-01): out-of-state CPAs serving Indiana-based clients and reciprocal applicants are deemed substantially equivalent if they passed the Uniform CPA Exam and licensed via any of three pathways (post-bacc + 1 yr; 150-hr bacc + 1 yr; bacc <150 hrs + 2 yrs). The policy is expressly non-binding guidance ('if it conflicts with these rules or laws, the rules or laws shall control'). Implementing rulemaking LSA #26-18 (amends/repeals portions of 872 IAC 1-1, 'Pathways to certified public accountant licensure') is mid-flight: authorized 2026-01-12, comment period closed 2026-02-27, public hearing 2026-03-13; final adoption not confirmed as of 2026-07-31. UPDATE (verifier): HB 1147 (2026) -> P.L. 25-2026, signed 2026-02-24, amends IC 25-2.1-3-2 (exam eligibility - baccalaureate w/ accounting concentration or board-determined equivalent) with provisions effective 2026-07-01 and 2027-01-01; browser confirmation of the enrolled text (HB1147.04.ENRS.pdf) still needed to rule out any reach into IC 25-2.1-4-10 mobility or firm chapters - rule_changes_on kept 2027-01-01 on the verifier's reading that the 2026-07-01 provision touches only exam-sitting eligibility. LSA Document #26-18 (872 IAC 1-1 pathways rulemaking) was approved post-hearing with AG and Governor sign-off and published in the Indiana Register, effective 2027-01-01 per INCPAS Vision-2027 guidance; the researcher's "final adoption not confirmed" caveat is superseded.

events.citation: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87B(h)(2)-(3); § 87D(a), (m); § 87B1/2(k); St. 2020, c. 319 (Act Modernizing Public Accountancy, approved 2021-01-11)
events.detail: S.209 -> S.2946 'An Act relative to modernizing the pathway to becoming a certified public accountant' passed the Senate 37-0 on 2026-02-12 and has sat in House Ways and Means since 2026-02-17 (House companion H.4356, new draft of H.352, reported favorably 2025-08-07, also in House W&M). NOT ENACTED as of 2026-07-31 -- which is the last day of the 194th General Court's formal sessions, so it either completes passage imminently or dies/carries to informal sessions. If enacted as Senate-engrossed, SECTION 5 strikes the NASBA-NQAS language from 87B(h)(2) and replaces it with individual criteria (valid other-state CPA license + education/experience of 87A1/2(e) + passed Uniform CPA Exam, with grandfather for anyone holding a valid certificate on or before 2025-12-31); no-notice/no-fee language is retained. Effective-date clause is SECTION 6, a flat 'This act shall take effect on January 1, 2027' -- no supermajority-conditioned immediate-effect option exists in the bill, so no vote-count check is applicable. The 2027-01-01 date in rule_changes_on is CONTINGENT on enactment.

events.citation: D.C. Official Code § 47-2853.49 (substantial equivalency; practice privilege); § 47-2853.44 (registration of firms of certified public accountants); 17 DCMR §§ 2541, 2542, 2546, 2548, 2550
events.detail:
TWO independent flux drivers, both live as of 2026-07-31.

(1) PENDING LEGISLATION. B26-494, the "Accountancy Practice Amendment Act of 2025" (Mayor-introduced), passed First Reading 2026-06-30 and Final Reading 2026-07-14 by 12-0 with 1 abstention (13-member Council). It adds a baccalaureate+2-years pathway AND rewrites mobility. The DC Board of Accountancy chairman's own written testimony (dlcp.dc.gov, hearing of 2026-03-26) states the UAA amendment it adopts "replaces the 'substantial equivalent' standard that states had applied with the 'individual-based standard'" -- i.e. DC's equivalence_test is set to move from nasba_state_level to individual_criteria / CPA=CPA. As of 2026-07-31 the bill had NOT yet been transmitted to the Mayor; after signature it must still complete the 30-legislative-day congressional review under D.C. Code § 1-206.02(c)(1) before becoming law. No operative date exists yet, so rule_changes_on is null rather than guessed.

EFFECTIVE-DATE PRECISION NOTE: DC permanent acts have no supermajority immediate-effect option; the operative date is set by congressional review, not by the vote count. DC EMERGENCY acts, by contrast, require a two-thirds vote and take effect IMMEDIATELY on mayoral signature for 90 days with no congressional review.

(2) EMERGENCY ACT ALREADY AT THE MAYOR'S DESK. B26-730, the "Business Licensing Reform and Accountancy Practice Emergency Amendment Act of 2026", passed Final Reading 2026-07-14 by 13-0 (unanimous; 13 of 13 members elected, comfortably above the two-thirds emergency threshold of 9) and was transmitted to the Mayor on 2026-07-29 with a response due 2026-08-12. Its companion Emergency Declaration Resolution was adopted 2026-07-14 as R26-0487. If signed, this emergency act takes effect immediately and could change the mobility rule within days of this verified_date, ahead of the permanent act. I could NOT read B26-730's text (see data_gap_note), so I cannot confirm which accountancy sections it amends. THIS RECORD SHOULD BE RE-VERIFIED AFTER 2026-08-12.

(3) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (statute vs. still-compiled rule) on firm registration for non-attest/tax services -- see notes. Statute § 47-2853.44(a)(4) exempts; unrepealed 2004 rules 17 DCMR 2542.1/2546.1/2546.3 require a permit of every nonresident firm. Conservative value recorded. UPDATE (verifier): add D.C. Law L26-0078, the Revised Business Licensing Reform Temporary Amendment Act of 2025 (effective 2025-12-31, EXPIRES 2026-08-13) as the driver explaining B26-730's timing and the 2026-08-12 mayoral deadline; if B26-730 is signed by 2026-08-12, schedule a SECOND re-check ~mid-November 2026 for reversion and search for a companion temporary act then. Effective-date reasoning CONFIRMED as correct and retained verbatim: both the congressional-review analysis for permanent acts and the two-thirds-of-13-elected (=9) emergency threshold analysis check out, and rule_changes_on=null (refusing to guess) was the right call. HIGHEST-RISK MISREADING, preserved: the Board's 2025-12-12 / 2026-01-15 substantial-equivalency advisory does NOT rewrite the 47-2853.49 practice-privilege test (it cites only 47-2853.08 and 17 DCMR 2508). Minor: the Board page links to nasba.org/licensure/mobility2/, not cpamobility.org. DiffLab: drop/de-weight the two lims.dccouncil.gov URLs (JS-only SPA behind a token-gated API - will silently never diff); add the Committee on Public Works and Operations page for B26-494 (heard 2026-03-26).

events.citation: 22 GCA § 35122 (Substantial Equivalency), Guam Accountancy Act of 2003; firm permits at 22 GCA § 35107; implementing rules at 25 GAR §§ 2103(d), 2106, 2112
events.detail: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on notice_required and fee_required (no pending legislation). (1) The codified statute, 22 GCA § 35122(a)(1) and (a)(2), states the privilege is automatic and that 'no notice or other submission shall be provided by any such individual.' (2) The Board's own official form, 'Notice of Intent to Practice Public Accountancy in Guam under Substantial Equivalency Provisions of 22 GCA §35122 and 25 GAR §2112' (https://www.guamboa.org/pdf/GU_SE.pdf, HTTP Last-Modified 2019-12-07, i.e. republished THREE YEARS AFTER the no-notice language was enacted), is a notarized filing requiring submission 'within 30 days after accepting an engagement.' (3) The compiled administrative rule 25 GAR § 2103(d)(2) prescribes fees expressly keyed to '22 GCA, § 35122': Initial $225.00, Renewal (annually) $175.00, Reactivation/Reinstatement $275.00, Provisional $175.00. A per-registrant annual renewal fee is only coherent if a registration/notice exists. Both the no-notice statutory language AND the substantial-equivalency fee schedule were enacted by the SAME act, P.L. 33-193 (Dec. 15, 2016), which repealed and reenacted both 22 GCA ch. 35 and 25 GAR ch. 2 — so this is an unresolved internal conflict within enacted Guam law, not a stale rule lagging a new statute. Per the conservative-value rule, notice_required and fee_required are recorded TRUE (the reading requiring more of the practitioner). A secondary, lesser divergence: the Board FAQ Q7 describes an open 'Individual Mobility' privilege for a CPA licensed 'in any other of the 54 U.S. jurisdictions,' which is broader than the statute's NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalence test; currently harmless because all jurisdictions are NQAS substantially equivalent, but it would diverge if any jurisdiction lost that status. No changeover date applies: Guam has enacted no accountancy amendment since 2016.

events.citation: MCL 339.727a (individual practice privilege, no notice/fee); MCL 339.728(1), (4), (5) (firm licensure trigger = in-state office; no-license out-of-state firm practice incl. attest); MCL 339.729(2) (peer review condition); MCL 339.734a (conditions of privilege). Occupational Code, 1980 PA 299, Art. 7.
events.detail: HB 4893 (2025-26 session) rewrites the licensure pathways in MCL 339.725 AND the 727a mobility equivalency test: new-language 727a would recognize licenses from jurisdictions requiring the uniform CPA exam plus any of three education/experience combos (150hr+1yr; post-baccalaureate accounting degree+1yr; 120hr/bachelor's+2yr), with a grandfather clause for individuals holding valid licenses as of 2024-12-31. Status: passed House 93-9 on 2025-11-12; referred to Senate Regulatory Affairs Committee 2025-12-02; still awaiting Senate hearing per MICPA update of 2026-03-17; NOT enacted -- compiled MCL current through PA 16 of 2026 (rendered 2026-06-13) still shows the existing 727a text. The bill's own effective-date clause reads 'This amendatory act takes effect 90 days after the date it is enacted into law,' so no changeover date exists yet (rule_changes_on null; the supermajority immediate-effect check is moot until enactment). SECOND flux item (stale board page): a legacy LARA 'CPA Firms' page (old CMS URL 0,4601,7-154-89334_72600_72602_72731_72855_91572-358925--,00.html) still serves the PRE-2018 version of section 728, which required firm licensure when a firm without a Michigan office performed audit/prospective-financial-examination/PCAOB engagements for a client with its home office in Michigan, and allowed only review/compilation without a license. PA 81 of 2018 (eff. 2018-06-17) repealed that home-office trigger; current 728(5) allows attest without a license. The board's current firm guide (rev 2026-01-26) and PA 81 notice match the current statute; the stale page is legacy content but still publicly served and surfaces in search results. UPDATE (verifier): TWO additional pending Senate bills introduced 2026-07-15 (Sen. Moss, Senate Regulatory Affairs) directly touch the answered sections: SB 1112 amends MCL 339.724 + 339.728 (temporary permit + the FIRM LICENSURE section under firm_registration_attest/tax) and SB 1113 amends MCL 339.725 + 339.727a + 339.729 (pathways, the PRACTICE-PRIVILEGE section itself, and peer review; apparent Senate counterpart to HB 4893). Scope correction: engrossed HB 4893 (H-2) amends 339.725, 727a AND 729. Currency: compiled MCL current through PA 20 of 2026 with 727a unchanged; MICPA confirmed HB 4893 still in Senate Regulatory Affairs as of 2026-06-09. Third-party aggregator claims that HB 4893 'became law 12/02/2025' are FALSE (that date was committee referral; no PA number exists). 2025 MR 18 accountancy admin-rule update (eff. 2025-09-29) checked - immaterial to recorded fields.

events.citation: 4 CMC §§ 3401-3440 (Accountancy Act of 2002, PL 13-52), esp. 4 CMC § 3401 (definitions), § 3422 (issuance/renewal of certificates), § 3423 (firm permits to practice); NMIAC §§ 1-10-801 (interstate practice), 1-10-2301 to 1-10-2310 (substantial equivalency/notification), 1-10-1605 (fees)
events.detail: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (not a pending legislative change). The CNMI's codified statute contains NO practice-privilege / substantial-equivalency mobility provision at all. The full text of PL 13-52 (Accountancy Act of 2002) was read section-by-section (Sections 1-24): Section 6 (codified 4 CMC § 3422) is titled 'Issuance and Renewal of Certificates' and provides only certificate-by-RECIPROCITY (the applicant applies for and is issued a CNMI certificate); Section 7 (codified 4 CMC § 3423) is firm permits. No section of the Act grants a practice privilege. HOWEVER, the Board's compiled administrative rules repeatedly presuppose a statutory substantial-equivalency standard that does not exist: NMIAC § 1-10-801(a)(2)(i) tells out-of-state individuals they may render services 'pursuant to: (i) Substantial equivalence (see section 6 of the Act [4 CMC § 3422])', NMIAC § 1-10-801(b) refers to 'the substantial equivalency standard set out in the Act, section 6 [4 CMC § 3422]', and NMIAC § 1-10-801(c)(3)-(4) requires notice/consent 'as required for substantially equivalent practitioners under section 6 of the Act [4 CMC § 3422]'. 4 CMC § 3422 as codified by the CNMI Law Revision Commission contains no such standard. The rules appear to have been drafted from the 2004+ UAA model against a statute that was never amended to match. This markup/contradiction was checked: the codified § 3422 (Source: PL 13-52, § 6, modified) and the original enrolled PL 13-52 Section 6 were compared line-by-line and AGREE with each other — so this is not a lost-strikethrough artifact; it is a genuine statute-vs-compiled-rule conflict. Conservative values recorded throughout: privilege treated as existing but conditioned on notice AND fee AND discretionary Board authorization; firm permit required for both attest and tax. No 2025-26 licensure/mobility wave legislation or rulemaking was found for CNMI — the Commonwealth Register is current through Vol. 48 (July 2026) with no Board of Accountancy entries, and the accountancy rules are still the 2007-adopted set as compiled in 2016. UPDATE (verifier - individual_practice_privilege REFUTED true -> set null): NO STATUTE GRANTS A PRACTICE PRIVILEGE. Full-text search of the enrolled PL 13-52 AND the codified 4 CMC 3401/3422/3423 (both downloaded and text-extracted) returns ZERO hits for "substantial equivalen", "practice privilege", or "principal place of business". Codified 4 CMC 3422 is captioned "Issuance and Renewal of Certificates" and 3422(c) provides only that "The Board shall issue a certificate to a holder of a certificate, license, or permit issued by another state upon a showing that:" - that is RECIPROCITY (get a CNMI certificate), not mobility. The sole basis for any privilege is a DISCRETIONARY board rule, NMIAC 1-10-801(c): "the Board MAY authorize the individual to exercise practice privileges in the CNMI provided the individual meets each of the following requirements" - permission on application, not an as-of-right privilege - and it rests on a thin statutory hook. The statute cuts the other way: 4 CMC 3422(a) provides "The holder of a certificate issued under this section may only practice public accountancy in a firm that holds a permit issued under section 3423 of this Act." A permissive true would tell a CPA a privilege exists where the profession's own authority treats CNMI as a non-mobility jurisdiction. null (not_verified) is the honest value: apply to the Board. No CNMI mobility legislation since (Commonwealth Register current through Vol. 48, July 2026, no Board of Accountancy entries; latest public laws PL 24-33/34/35 July 2026, none accountancy).

events.citation: ORS 673.153 (holders of licenses issued by other states); ORS 673.160 (registration of business organizations); ORS 673.455 (peer review); ORS 673.010(20) ("Substantially equivalent") -- all as amended by Or. Laws 2025 ch. 132 (SB 797), effective 2026-01-01; implementing rules OAR 801-005-0010, 801-010-0080, 801-010-0345, 801-050-0020 (BOA 1-2026, filed 01/29/2026, eff. 02/01/2026)
events.detail: Oregon is mid-wave and has multiple live moving parts. (1) STATUTORY CHANGEOVER ALREADY OPERATIVE: SB 797 (2025) = Or. Laws 2025 ch. 132 rewrote ORS 673.010(20), 673.153, 673.160 and 673.455. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED ON THE ACT ITSELF: the enrolled act runs SECTION 1 through SECTION 39 with NO effective-date section, NO operative-date section and NO emergency clause (verified by reading all 26 pages of the enrolled PDF, including pages 25-26; no '2026' string appears anywhere in the act). Oregon Const. Art. IV sec. 28 sets only a 90-day floor, but the operative default is statutory: ORS 171.022 -- 'an Act of the Legislative Assembly takes effect on January 1 of the year after passage.' 2025 regular session adjourned sine die 2025-06-27. Legislative Counsel's own ORS annotation confirms the date by printing the editorial gloss 'the effective date of this 2025 Act [January 1, 2026]' in the Note following ORS 673.410. Therefore rule_changes_on = 2026-01-01. No supermajority/immediate-effect analysis was needed because the act contains no such option. (2) BOARD RULE CHANGEOVER: BOA 1-2026, amend filed 01/29/2026, effective 02/01/2026, conformed OAR ch. 801 to SB 797. Materially, it DELETED the old mobility subsection (1) of OAR 801-010-0080 and retitled that rule 'Applications by Reciprocity' -- confirmed by the OSCPA comment published on the board's own past-rulemaking page ('The proposed draft removes subsection (1) but retains subsection (4) (renumbered as subsection (2))... the omission of subsection (1) eliminates explicit OAR language on mobility'). Net effect: individual mobility now rests on ORS 673.153 alone, with no implementing OAR. (3) OPEN RULEMAKING RIGHT NOW: the board's rulemaking page states rulemaking began June 4 with rule exposure 2026-07-01 and a public comment period running 2026-07-01 through 9:00 a.m. 2026-09-24. The exposed rule list is not published on that page, so it is unknown whether mobility/firm-registration rules are in scope. The same page also flags board/LRC policy work on private-equity ownership of CPA firms, which would touch ORS 673.160 firm requirements. (4) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON FIRM-REGISTRATION SCOPE: OAR 801-010-0345(3) requires out-of-state firms serving Oregon clients to register if they perform 'Attestation engagements' or PCAOB engagements. 'Attestation services' under ORS 673.010(1) and the board's own OAR 801-005-0010 definition includes SSARS reviews (para. (b)) and other SSAE examination/review/agreed-upon-procedures work (para. (d)). But ORS 673.160(1)(c) triggers registration ONLY for 673.010(1)(a) SAS audits, (c) SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and (e) PCAOB engagements, and ORS 673.160(3)(a) expressly EXEMPTS out-of-state firms doing 673.010(1)(b)/(d) work and compilations. The board's own peer-review web page follows the narrower statutory reading ('Out-of-state firms performing compilation and/or review services for Oregon clients are not required to register with the Board'). The compiled rule is therefore BROADER than the statute. Because both sources answer firm_registration_attest 'true', the conservative value is recorded either way; the disagreement affects only which engagement types trigger it, and the conservative (rule-based, broader) reading is described in notes. (5) STALE BOARD WEB GUIDANCE: the board's licensee-FAQ page and its License Application Requirements page still cite 'substantial equivalency as defined in ORS 673.010(21)' -- that is the PRE-2026 cross-reference that SB 797 sec. 12 struck out of ORS 673.153(1) and renumbered; the current definition sits at ORS 673.010(20) with new three-pathway criteria. OAR 801-010-0080's 'Statutes/Other Implemented' line still lists ORS 673.040, which SB 797 sec. 37 REPEALED. These are stale-citation defects, not substantive conflicts, but they show board guidance trailing the statute. UPDATE (verifier - rule_changes_on CLEARED to null, per the Puerto Rico precedent): the recorded 2026-01-01 is the SB 797 changeover, seven months in the past and fully in force - a forward-looking changeover field holding a past date reads to any consumer as "a change is coming" and would make downstream alerts fire on completed history. The completed changeover is recorded here instead; rule_in_flux stays TRUE because Board rulemaking implementing SB 797 is live with a decision point expected around late September 2026. SEPARATELY, correcting the researcher's timing gloss: SB 1510 is ALREADY EFFECTIVE (on or about 2026-06-05) and created the Registered Enrolled Agent credential - it is not a prospective 2027 tax-side change. The substantive conclusions are unchanged.

events.citation: Ley Núm. 293 de 15 de mayo de 1945, según enmendada ("Ley de Contabilidad Pública de 1945"), Sec. 4 (20 L.P.R.A. § 775) [privilegio de ejercer / equivalencia sustancial]; Sec. 5 (20 L.P.R.A. § 778) [registro de firmas]; Sec. 6 (20 L.P.R.A. § 779) [licencias]; Sec. 18(12) (20 L.P.R.A. § 772) [definición de "Práctica de la Contabilidad Pública"]; as last amended by Ley Núm. 174-2025 (P. del S. 642, approved 19 Dec 2025)
events.detail: Ley Núm. 174-2025 (P. del S. 642), approved 2025-12-19 and certified by the Departamento de Estado on 2025-12-23, amends ONLY Sección 3 of Ley 293-1945 (the education/experience licensure pathways -- it adds the bachelor's + 2 years supervised experience route, i.e. Puerto Rico's participation in the 2025-26 national pathway wave). Its Artículo 4 (Vigencia) reads: 'El Artículo 3 de esta Ley comenzará a regir inmediatamente después de su aprobación y el resto de los Artículos comenzarán a regir a noventa (90) días después de su aprobación.' Artículo 3 is a rulemaking mandate and took effect immediately on 2025-12-19; the substantive Artículo 1 (the new Sección 3) took effect 90 days after approval = 2026-03-19. There is no supermajority/immediate-effect condition in this act, so no final-passage vote count needed to fix the date. CRITICALLY: the act does NOT touch Sección 4 (practice privilege / equivalencia sustancial), Sección 5 (firm registration) or Sección 6 (licenses) -- the mobility text quoted here is unchanged and traces to the 'mobility' amendment Ley Núm. 147-2014. Flagged in flux anyway because (a) Artículo 3 of Ley 174-2025 orders the Junta to 'adopta[r] o enmienda[r] todos los reglamentos que sean necesarios para cumplir las disposiciones de esta Ley' and no such new reglamento has appeared on the Board's page (it still lists only Ethics Reg. 8383/2013, Continuing Education Reg. 8381/2013 and 9447/2023, and Reasonable Accommodation Reg. 8644/2015), so an implementing rule is pending; and (b) the changed licensure pathways feed directly into the substantial-equivalency test Sección 4 depends on. rule_changes_on records the 2026-03-19 changeover of Ley 174-2025. UPDATE (verifier - rule_changes_on CLEARED to null): the recorded 2026-03-19 changeover is CONSUMMATED HISTORY, not a pending change. Ley 174-2025 was approved 2025-12-19; its Articulo 4 reads verbatim "El Articulo 3 de esta Ley comenzara a regir inmediatamente despues de su aprobacion y el resto de los Articulos comenzaran a regir a noventa (90) dias despues de su aprobacion" (Departamento de Estado certified copy, "Certifico que es copia fiel y exacta del original", 23 de diciembre de 2025). 19 Dec + 90 days = 19 Mar 2026 - arithmetic correct, no supermajority condition to check - but that date is 4.5 months BEFORE this record's verified_date and the compiled text already carries the amendment (Rev. 29 May 2026 Sec. 3(e)(3) 120-hour bachelor's + two-years route and new Sec. 3(h) experience block, neither present in the pre-amendment codified Sec. 774). Pointing a forward-looking changeover field at a completed change would make downstream alerts fire on something that already happened. rule_in_flux stays TRUE on the pending Articulo 3 rulemaking.

events.detail: UPDATE (verifier - rule_in_flux CORRECTED false -> true): the recorded false rested on two materially FALSE assertions, both deleted below. No PRIMARY evidence of a pending change exists (the VI Legislature bill tracker is clean of accountancy bills post-2014 and the Board Rules retrieved are the October 2015 originals), so this is not a known changeover - but false is not affirmatively supportable either, because the Board demonstrably RULEMAKES on mobility (Board Rules Section Seven, "PRACTICE PRIVILEGE/MOBILITY", Rules 7.1-7.7), which is precisely the Nevada/Arkansas board-rule channel this record claimed to have ruled out. Secondary reporting (300hours.com, uncorroborated by any primary source) states the Board "is working to update its rules to create additional pathways to CPA licensure and individual mobility consistent with the Uniform Accountancy Act, but no new pathway has been enacted" - pointing at the same blind spot. Treat USVI as watch-the-board, not settled.
